# The documented command line of the PostgreSQL dump program, release 17,
# written from its reference page (app-pgdump). Options of one release: a
# newer one is added here when the manual gains it.
  -f, --file=FILENAME             output file or directory name
  -F, --format=c|d|t|p            output file format
  -j, --jobs=NUM                  dump this many tables at once
  -v, --verbose                   verbose mode
  -V, --version                   print the release
  -Z, --compress=METHOD           compression of the output
  --lock-wait-timeout=TIMEOUT     fail after waiting this long for a table lock
  --no-sync                       do not wait for the files to reach disk
  -a, --data-only                 dump only the data, not the schema
  -b, --large-objects             include large objects
  -B, --no-large-objects          exclude large objects
  --blobs                         older name of --large-objects
  --no-blobs                      older name of --no-large-objects
  -c, --clean                     emit commands that drop objects first
  -C, --create                    emit commands that create the database
  -e, --extension=PATTERN         dump only the matching extensions
  -E, --encoding=ENCODING         dump in this encoding
  -n, --schema=PATTERN            dump only the matching schemas
  -N, --exclude-schema=PATTERN    do not dump the matching schemas
  -O, --no-owner                  skip restoration of object ownership
  -s, --schema-only               dump only the schema, not the data
  -S, --superuser=NAME            superuser name for disabling triggers
  -t, --table=PATTERN             dump only the matching tables
  -T, --exclude-table=PATTERN     do not dump the matching tables
  -x, --no-privileges             do not dump privileges
  --binary-upgrade                for use by upgrade utilities only
  --column-inserts                dump data as INSERT with column names
  --attribute-inserts             older name of --column-inserts
  --disable-dollar-quoting        quote bodies with standard string syntax
  --disable-triggers              disable triggers during a data-only restore
  --enable-row-security           dump content of tables with row security
  --exclude-table-data=PATTERN    do not dump data of the matching tables
  --extra-float-digits=NUM        override the digits of floating point output
  --if-exists                     use IF EXISTS when dropping objects
  --include-foreign-data=PATTERN  dump data of the matching foreign servers
  --inserts                       dump data as INSERT commands
  --load-via-partition-root       load partitions through the root table
  --no-comments                   do not dump comments
  --no-publications               do not dump publications
  --no-security-labels            do not dump security labels
  --no-subscriptions              do not dump subscriptions
  --no-table-access-method        do not dump table access methods
  --no-tablespaces                do not dump tablespace assignments
  --no-toast-compression          do not dump TOAST compression methods
  --no-unlogged-table-data        do not dump data of unlogged tables
  --on-conflict-do-nothing        add ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to inserts
  --quote-all-identifiers         quote every identifier
  --rows-per-insert=NROWS         rows in one INSERT command
  --section=SECTION               dump the named section
  --serializable-deferrable       wait for a moment with no anomalies
  --snapshot=SNAPSHOT             use the given synchronized snapshot
  --strict-names                  require every pattern to match something
  --use-set-session-authorization set ownership with SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION
  --filter=FILENAME               read include and exclude rules from a file
  --exclude-extension=PATTERN     do not dump the matching extensions
  --sequence-data                 dump sequence data even in schema-only mode
  -d, --dbname=DBNAME             database to dump
  -h, --host=HOSTNAME             server host or socket directory
  -p, --port=PORT                 server port
  -U, --username=NAME             user name to connect as
  -w, --no-password               never prompt for a password
  -W, --password                  force a password prompt
  --role=ROLENAME                 role set before the dump
